title: fix(plugin-form): a failed read no longer keeps a record form on its error screen after a later read of the same kind succeeds (objectui#10682)
body:
Refs #10682

Clause-②: no

PR 1 of 2 for objectui#10682: the six record forms. The card's `LineItemsPanel` row (folded in from objectui#10683) is not in this PR. It rides PR 2, after PR objectui#10650 (which edits that file), and PR 2 carries the card's closing reference. No export, schema, prop or accept set moves. Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 5, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01KUxVUa7e39aNjhkKi1gsoy`.

## What changed

Every layout `ObjectForm` routes to renders its error screen ahead of the form whenever its load error is set. Each kept ONE `error` state that its two reads wrote, the object schema (`getObjectSchema`) and the record (`findOne`), and nothing cleared it: 13 writes and 0 clears across the six files on base `7afc81d`.

Each form now keeps the failure of each read apart, through one private helper, `packages/plugin-form/src/loadFailure.ts` (not re-exported from `index.tsx`):

- `beginLoadRun(seqRef, setFailures, source)` numbers a run of one read (`schema` or `record`) and hands back `fail(err)` and `commit()`. Both are no-ops once a newer run of that read has begun. This is the run-sequence shape PR objectui#10680 gave `ObjectTimeline`, kept per read.
- `shownLoadFailure(failures)` is what the error screen reports: the schema failure first, else the record failure.

In each form, the one `useState` for `error` became a per-read failure pair plus a run-number ref, and `error` is now derived from them. The render is unchanged. Each fetch effect begins a run in its body. Its commit branches call `commit()` and its failure branches call `fail()`:

| form | schema read: commit / fail | record read: commit / fail |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ObjectForm` (default arm) | the read, the inline-members fallback in the `catch`, the inline branch with no object or data source / the `catch` | the read, the create-mode seed / the `catch`, the missing-data-source report |
| `DrawerForm`, `ModalForm`, `SplitForm` | the read / the `catch` | the read, the create-mode seed, the no-data-source seed / the `catch` |
| `TabbedForm`, `WizardForm` | the read / the `catch` | the read, the seed branch / the `catch` |

**Why per read (H2).** One slot fed by two reads cannot follow the triage's rule by clearing it on either commit. A single slot that remembers WHICH read set it is not enough either: when both reads fail, it keeps only the later failure, and that read's success then clears it while the other failure still holds. After a failed schema read, a record read can run only over a schema already in state for another object or data source, because every form gates its record read on `objectSchema`. Clearing there would draw the new record against the old object's fields with no report. So each read keeps its own failure, a read's commit clears only its own, and the error screen shows while either is set.

**Why a helper (H3).** The six copies were the same writes. The helper is the one place that numbers runs and chooses which failure shows. It is a module function over a `useState` setter and a `useRef` that each component declares, not a custom hook. `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` treats both as stable, so no fetch effect gains a dependency, and no dependency list changed (see Boundary).

**What the run guard covers.** Only the failure writes are scoped. The values each run commits are written as before. `DrawerForm`, `ModalForm`, `SplitForm` and `TabbedForm` already guard their record read with a `cancelled` flag. `ObjectForm`'s record read, `WizardForm`'s record read and every schema read had no guard (see Acceptance notes for the values race that leaves).

**Does a failed BACKGROUND re-read keep the last good values? (H4)** No, on all six. No form has a silent mode. The failure is reported, the last good values stay in state but are not drawn, and the next re-read that succeeds takes the screen back. The default arm's background re-read is the data-invalidation bus (objectui#10572). The five other layouts do not subscribe to the bus (measured below). Theirs is a host re-render that rebuilds `initialValues`, which re-runs their record read in place. The pin states this per form.

## Premise readings (H1)

- **The error lifecycle holds on all six.** On the base sources, a record read that fails and then a later record read that succeeds leave the error screen up on every layout (6 of 6 red, below). The filed probe's bus path on the default arm is red too.
- **The bus trigger holds only for the default arm.** A throwaway probe (not committed) mounted each layout through `object-form` in edit mode, let the first read succeed, then sent `notifyDataChanged({ objectName: '*' })`. `findOne` calls went 1 → 2 on the default arm, and 1 → 1 on `drawer`, `modal`, `split`, `tabbed` and `wizard`. For those five the pin's second read comes from a record swap or a host re-render.

## Pin: `recordFormsErrorClears-10682.test.tsx`

One enumeration over the six layouts in `packages/plugin-form/src/`. Each layout is reached through the real `SchemaRenderer` and this package's `object-form` registration. Every `getObjectSchema` and `findOne` is held open by hand. There are 9 cases per layout, plus the filed probe's bus path on the default arm: 55 cases.

- Base leg: the pin, written before any source edit, run against the untouched base sources: `exit=1`, `Tests 21 failed | 34 passed (55)`.
- Head leg at `d41377b`: `exit=0`, `Tests 55 passed (55)`.

| case | base / head |
|:--|:--|
| lit control: a form that never failed draws its record and no error screen | green / green on all six |
| a record read fails, then a later record read succeeds: the value is shown and the error screen is gone | **RED** / green on all six |
| a failed background re-read over good values is reported; the next re-read that succeeds takes the screen back | **RED** / green on all six |
| per source: a schema read fails, then a RECORD read succeeds: the schema error stays | green / green on all six (red under A1) |
| control: a record read fails, then another fails: the newer failure is shown | green / green on all six |
| a superseded record read that fails does not raise the error screen over the current record | **RED** / green on default and wizard; green / green on the four with `cancelled` |
| a superseded record read that succeeds does not clear the current failure | green / green on all six (red under A2 on default and wizard) |
| a superseded schema read that fails does not raise the error screen over the current object | **RED** / green on all six |
| a superseded schema read that succeeds does not clear the current schema failure | green / green on all six (red under A2) |
| default arm only: a record read fails, then a bus re-read succeeds | **RED** / green |

## Ablations

Base cannot redden the rows that guard against a clear, because base never clears. Their red legs are ablations of `loadFailure.ts` on the committed head `d41377b`, each through the objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. Each anchor hit once, each landing is proven by an anchor count of 1 → 0 and a blob change from `d854a66b6c46`, and each restore by blob == HEAD (`d854a66b6c46`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. No build step is involved: the pin loads this package's sources through relative imports, and `@object-ui/react` resolves to its `src` through the root vitest alias.

- **A1**, the per-read split removed: `commit()` clears BOTH failures (the single-slot "clear on any commit" shape). `Tests 6 failed | 49 passed (55)`: exactly the six per-source rows.
- **A2**, `commit()` without its current-run check. `8 failed | 47 passed`: the superseded schema success row on all six, and the superseded record success row on default and wizard. The other four stay green because their `cancelled` flag returns before the commit.
- **A3**, `fail()` without its current-run check. `8 failed | 47 passed`: the superseded schema failure row on all six, and the superseded record failure row on default and wizard.

## Local verification (HEAD `45086fa`, after merging `origin/main` at `69a6fc1`)

- Dependency closure: `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-form^...' --concurrency=2` at `a172199`: `Tasks: 11 successful, 11 total`. The last merge (`a172199` to `45086fa`) brought only `app-shell` and `plugin-chatbot` files and two changesets, outside that closure; the type-check below runs `^build` again at `45086fa`.

The pin is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program and `loadFailure.ts` in `tsconfig.json`'s (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit each).

Neither describes the load-error lifecycle, so both still hold.
- Lint, narrowed to the 8 changed files: `eslint.config.js` lints `**/*.{ts,tsx}` and declares no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so no type-aware rule runs and this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The `--format json` output counted 8 files and 0 errors. The six sources carry 55, 22, 20, 9, 8 and 21 warnings on head (`ObjectForm`, `DrawerForm`, `ModalForm`, `SplitForm`, `TabbedForm`, `WizardForm`), equal to their base blobs, with the same multiset of rule and headline. `loadFailure.ts` carries 0, and the pin 7 (`no-explicit-any`, the sibling pins' pattern).
- NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`, reason: it exits 1 with "388 self-import(s) could not be judged", each "type entry `./dist/index.d.ts` is not on disk -- run `pnpm build` first" for packages outside this closure (a missing prerequisite, not a verdict). This diff touches no README and no export.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:sdui-registration-pins`, reason: it needs a console build. This diff touches no registration and no `sideEffects` field. CI builds the console and runs it.

## Boundary

- No changed line in the six sources touches a dependency list or a `useEffect(`, `useCallback(` or `useMemo(` call (grep over the diff: 0 hits). The removed lines are exactly the six `error` states and the 13 writes.
- `index.tsx` is untouched: no new export and no new prop.
- `LineItemsPanel.tsx` is untouched.
- Files: `ObjectForm.tsx` +37/-4, `DrawerForm.tsx` +31/-3, `ModalForm.tsx` +31/-3, `SplitForm.tsx` +31/-3, `TabbedForm.tsx` +29/-3, `WizardForm.tsx` +30/-3; new `loadFailure.ts` (85 lines) and the new pin (365 lines, 55 cases); `.changeset/10682-form-error-clears.md` (`'@object-ui/plugin-form': patch`).

## Acceptance notes

- **Reported to the seat, not changed here (values, not `error`).** The default arm and `WizardForm` write a superseded record read's VALUES over the current record's. Throwaway probe (not committed): the read of `r1` is held, the form re-renders to `r2`, `r2` answers "Two", then `r1` answers late. The default arm and wizard show `One (stale)`. Drawer, modal, split and tabbed show `Two`: their `cancelled` flag, pinned by `recordSwapLoading.test.tsx` for those four only. This PR's guard covers the failure writes only, and the values writes are byte-identical to base. The schema reads' `setObjectSchema` is unguarded on all six as well.
- **Reported to the seat.** The five non-default layouts do not re-read on the data-invalidation bus (probe above, 1 → 1). The pending changeset `.changeset/10572-plugin-form-reads-invalidation-bus.md` reads: "`object-form` in edit mode re-reads its record when the data-invalidation bus (`notifyDataChanged` from `@object-ui/react`) reports a change to that record, its object, or everything (objectui#10572)." Each of the five is an `object-form` with a `formType`.
- `LineItemsPanel`, the folded objectui#10683 row, stays for PR 2, after PR objectui#10650.
- A failed read whose later run neither reads nor seeds (the data source goes away, say) leaves the earlier failure on screen. The rule is "cleared when a later run of the same read commits", never at run start, as in objectui#10578.
- Consistency across the family: all six report a failed background re-read with no silent mode, as `ObjectTimeline`, `ObjectCalendar` and `ObjectKanban` do (PR objectui#10680). `ObjectGantt` and `ObjectMap` keep the last good rows.
